title: 7.1 Preparing to Track the Campaign
html:
Live Campaign · Pro Analytics · Business application

Preparing to Track the Campaign

Your Brand is the foundation. The Message Matrix turns that foundation into a focused campaign: a defined audience, serialized content and a useful path from each channel back to your website. Before publishing, decide what you want that audience to do and how you will recognize progress.

Pro Analytics brings supported website, email and social reporting into your company workspace on Social Media Magnet Pro. It does not require the old weekly-post plugin or access-token handshake on your customer website. Your website still needs working GA4 tracking; authorizing a connection does not install it.

Start with a Business Question

  • Awareness: Is useful content reaching the audience we intend to serve?
  • Acquisition: Are our spokes bringing relevant visitors into the Brand hub?
  • Retention: Are people returning, and does email give them a useful reason to come back?
  • Action: Are the intended form or phone events occurring, and what do they actually count?

Prepare the Workspace

  1. Open Pro Analytics and confirm the company. Owners working across companies should check the company name before every connection or report.
  2. In Account, save the website, logo, social profiles and intended service area. A saved profile link does not authorize that platform. A location entry records your market; it does not apply a geography filter.
  3. The Owner connects the correct GA4 property, selects Mailchimp or Constant Contact when used, and authorizes the intended Facebook Page and linked professional Instagram account when available. Confirm the displayed account names after saving.
  4. Confirm the event names used for forms and phone actions. Test the intended action with your website/analytics administrator before relying on the totals.
  5. Choose a baseline period and a reporting timezone. Record launch dates and meaningful changes in the publishing calendar.
  6. Invite only the people who need company access. Owners manage connections and team access; Owners and Analysts can request Reviews when enabled. Viewers can read shared results.

The four Brand elements—Story, Promise, Belief and Trust—remain your reference for every decision. A larger audience is useful only when your content and next action strengthen the relationship you are trying to build.

title: 7.3 Pro Analytics: Traffic Coming into the Website
html:
Live Campaign · Pro Analytics · Business application

Pro Analytics: Traffic Coming into the Website

Open Pro Analytics → Dashboard → Report. Confirm the company, then choose the dates that answer your question. The Report is a selected-period view of your campaign, rather than the old cumulative weekly grading report.

Select Dates and Compare

  1. Choose 30, 60 or 90 days, one year, or a custom range.
  2. Set Compare with to None, Prior period or Previous year. None shows the selected period without a directional comparison.
  3. Select Apply dates and wait for the report to finish. A changed field is not a completed refresh. Read the visible progress, missing-data or error message before interpreting results.
  4. Confirm the displayed dates, comparison and timezone. Use the same selection when printing or sharing.

Follow the Traffic Back to the Message

SourceInterpretation
Organic SearchVisits attributed to unpaid search results. Inspect the content and customer question behind the visit.
SocialVisits attributed to social channels. Compare the relevant post, link and hub destination.
EmailVisits attributed to an email campaign. Consistent campaign tags help distinguish the return path.
ReferralVisits attributed to links on other websites.
Direct / unattributedThe source is not clear. This can include typed/bookmarked visits and missing referral information; do not assign all Direct traffic to email or Brand awareness.

Use Sources and Timeline to see which channels contribute and when activity changes. A percentage should always be read with its count: growth from two visits to four is 100%, but it is still four visits. Check whether a comparison period had different publishing activity or a seasonal event.

Read the Brand Axis Signals

The dashboard plots session change vertically and change in the returning-to-new-user ratio horizontally. Goal events per 100 sessions are shown separately. These signals help you inspect acquisition and retention balance; they do not directly measure loyalty, sentiment or the reason a person returned. With Compare None, a centered marker does not prove ideal Brand alignment.

Filtering and Missing Data

GA4 automatically excludes known bots, but does not supply the excluded volume. Additional bot screening and service-area filtering are not active in this implementation. Saved service locations do not remove out-of-market visits. Unavailable data is not zero, and geography alone does not identify a bot.

Put It to Work

  1. Save a Report for one meaningful period.
  2. Identify the largest relevant source and one change over time.
  3. Inspect the actual message and destination before changing the campaign.
  4. Use Print / Save for the completed Report; retain the company, report type and timestamp in its filename.

title: 7.7 Progress Reports and Pro Analytics Reviews
html:
Live Campaign · Pro Analytics · Business application

Progress Reports and Pro Analytics Reviews

A useful progress report ends in a decision. Pro Analytics gives your company a shared view of results so the team can see what changed, check the content behind it and agree on the next move. Pro Analytics reporting does not grade your company against a class or campaign-population mean.

Report, Review and Account

WorkspacePurpose
ReportSelected-period website, email and supported social results. Change dates and comparisons, inspect the available sections, and print a completed snapshot.
ReviewSaved Pro Analytics Reviews and deliberate requests for a new interpretation of the selected evidence.
AccountCompany details, connections, service-area record, supporting Strategy Canvas/Brand Dyno documents, team access and available billing controls.

Use a Repeatable Business Rhythm

  1. Confirm company, dates, comparison and connection readiness. Wait for the Report to complete.
  2. Read traffic, acquisition/retention balance and goal events together.
  3. Choose two meaningful changes, then inspect the relevant posts, emails and hub pages.
  4. Note a limitation: missing attribution, short observation time, unverified event definition or unavailable provider data.
  5. Write three Moves to Make. Give each an audience, content focus, channel, hub destination, owner, publishing date and success measure.
  6. Return after an appropriate observation period and compare the next matched period. A weekly check can use a seven-day custom range; the platform is not limited to weekly reporting.

Request a Review Deliberately

An Owner or Analyst can request a new Pro Analytics Review when enabled. Use a valid comparison for directional analysis. Changing dates does not automatically create a Review. The company allowance applies to new requested Reviews; opening or printing an existing saved Review does not use another one. Check the allowance and status shown in the workspace.

If you have a Strategy Canvas or Brand Dyno report, an Owner or Analyst can upload it in Account as supporting foundation material before requesting a new Review. Previously saved Reviews retain the evidence used when they were created; uploading a new document does not rewrite them.

Turn the Review into Campaign Work

  • Read the current Brand Axis context and the distinct content signals.
  • Check recommendations against the Brand Story, Promise, Belief and Trust.
  • Use Develop, Reframe and Create to build a dimensional message sequence rather than repeating one generic promotion across all channels.
  • Put the Moves to Make into the Message Matrix and publishing calendar.
  • Use the Report to check the result later. The Review recommends; your team implements and verifies.

Save and Share

Open the intended saved Review before printing. Use the matching Print / Save control on Report or Review and confirm the company, type and timestamp in the filename. Include supporting results when useful. Printing should preserve readable text rather than a giant image of each page.

Put It to Work

  1. Schedule a team checkpoint.
  2. Agree on three Moves to Make.
  3. Assign responsibility and a follow-up date.

title: 7.8 Summary and Business Review
html:
Live Campaign · Pro Analytics · Business application

Summary and Business Review

Measurement should make the next campaign decision clearer. Establish a verified baseline, select a meaningful period, distinguish platform exposure from website behavior, and connect the findings to the Message Matrix and publishing calendar. The Brand foundation remains the reference for every move.

Key Terms

Selected reporting period · Prior period · Previous year · Session · User · Returning visitor · Source/medium · Campaign tag · Event · Key event · Goal events per 100 sessions · Lifetime response · Attribution · Measurement limitation · Pro Analytics Review · Moves to Make

Questions for Your Team

  • What business question does this date selection answer? Is the comparison appropriate?
  • What do the Pro Analytics Brand Axis signals measure, and what does it leave for content review or customer research?
  • Which social or email message deserves closer inspection, and why?
  • Are form and phone counts tracking the intended actions?
  • What can you Develop, Reframe or Create to strengthen the Brand and return path?
  • Who will publish the changes, and when will you check the result?

title: 12.2 Facebook User Displeasure Actually Leads to Less, but Better Organic Content
html:
Historical context: this section describes Facebook changes in 2016–2018. Its screenshots and menu references document that period. Use the Pro Analytics application below and the current channel interfaces for today’s workflow.

12.2 Facebook User Displeasure Actually Leads to Less, but Better Organic Content

At this stage, according to Social Flow, organic reach was still dropping at a rate of 42% between January and May of 20161.  Ironically, however, Facebook users noticed the trend of more and more ad content in their timeline news feeds, along with a plethora of uninteresting, low-quality organic posts.  Through both, Facebook users began voicing their displeasure as posts from businesses, brands, and media were crowding out the personal moments that led users to connect more with each other in the first place2.  Facebook realized they had to fix this saturation issue by changing the algorithm.  They needed to promote high-quality, personalized content to continue building meaningful relationships in the social space.

In the blog post announcing the algorithm change, Facebook Engineering Director Lars Backstrom indicated the new algorithm update would try to ensure that “stories posted directly by friends that you care about, such as photos, videos, status updates or links, will be higher up in the News Feed, so you are less likely to miss them.”  He also warned that Pages could anticipate a dip in organic reach and referral traffic for some pages and encouraged Pages to post things they know their audiences are likely to share with their friends3.  With this change, Social Flow adjusted their original report from 42% to a decrease of 52% from January to July of 20164.

Furthermore, Facebook doubled down on this commitment to friends and family in the next two years.  In 2017, Facebook did not change the algorithm but rather changed the News Feed function entirely.  In October, Facebook tested an ad-free News Feed that users could switch to, dedicated to publisher content rather than personal content. To businesses, it clearly foreshadowed a Facebook that separated business/brand content from friends/family content.  Today, that "alternative News Feed" is known as the "Pages" option on the left-hand sidebar of a user's News Feed5.

In 2018, Facebook again updated its News Feed algorithm.  This update did not eliminate Page content entirely but set different priorities on what would be posted to users’ News Feed.  Paul Armstrong provides a great article about a Facebook webinar that shared these priorities at Forbes.com6.  He highlights what Facebook prioritizes as important for News Feeds:

  • People sharing a link over Messenger
  • Commenting on or liking a person's photo or status updates
  • Multiple replies to a status update or photo = more likely to see again
  • Meaningful interactions - this doesn't mean 'like if you agree.'

He also notes that Facebook wants content publishers to have other people share their content with Facebook and not be the initial publisher of the content.  That means content creation on blog sites needs to have social posts buttons that allow users to post into space rather than posting it directly into the social space.  Facebook also provided additional tips for content publishers from this webinar.

Additional Tips for Content Publishers:

  • Have other people share your content on Facebook.
  • Start getting journalists to comment and spur on activity.
  • Focus on content that other people will share.
  • Create stories that can be updated.
  • Use paid media to create spikes on relevant content.
  • Start thinking about local products.
  • Start pushing the 'Follow' function for Pages.
  • Stop tagging.
  • Become engaged in Facebook Groups.

Finally, shares and comments, in particular, are considered "active" interactions, which Facebook considers more "meaningful" when slotting content on a user's News Feed. For that reason, video watch time, referral traffic, and organic reach might even decrease this year if the content does not create a meaningful interaction7.

 

References:

1. Social Flow.  Media Companies’ Facebook Reach Has Fallen 42% This Year.  http://www.socialflow.com/media-companies-facebook-reach-has-fallen-42-this-year/

2. NeilPatel.com.  Is Facebook Organic Reach Really Dead?  Here’s How to Break Through It for More Social Engagement.  https://neilpatel.com/blog/is-facebook-organic-reach-dead/

3. Facebook Newsroom.  Helping Make Sure You Don’t Miss Stories from Friends.  https://newsroom.fb.com/news/2016/06/news-feed-fyi-helping-make-sure-you-dont-miss-stories-from-friends/

4. MarketingLand.com.  Facebook Organic Reach Is Down 52% for Publishers’ Pages This Year.  https://marketingland.com/facebook-organic-reach-drop-steepens-52-publishers-pages-187253

5. HubSpot.  The Decline of Organic Facebook Reach & How to Adjust to the Algorithm.  https://blog.hubspot.com/marketing/facebook-organic-reach-declining

6. Forbes.com.  What You Should Know From Facebook’s Private Newsfeed Webinar.  https://www.forbes.com/sites/paularmstrongtech/2018/02/03/what-you-should-know-from-facebooks-private-newsfeed-webinar/#2315c5b4452d

7. Same as 5.

Apply This with Pro Analytics

The algorithm discussion above describes historical changes, not a current screen-by-screen setup guide or a fixed performance benchmark. For the current workflow, use Pro Analytics → Report and the available Facebook/Instagram native insights. Inspect views, engagement, source visits and goal events as distinct signals; then connect the conclusion to the actual content.
